cards.text: One of the Pharisees, the strictest group in the Jewish religion (Acts 26:5), invites Jesus to eat, and Jesus goes in and reclines at the table. A dinner invitation! The last one I got, friend, an angel had to dig me out of a junk drawer to deliver it.
Then a woman from that town finds out Jesus is dining there. The text calls her a sinful woman, and she comes to that house carrying something.

cards.question: What does the sinful woman bring with her to the Pharisee's house?

cards.text: She stands behind Jesus, right at His feet, and she's weeping. Her tears start falling on His feet.

cards.question: The woman wipes Jesus' feet with her own hair.
The woman kisses Jesus' feet. Then what does she do with her perfume?

answers.text: She anoints His feet with it
She pours it over His head
She hands it to the Pharisee

cards.text: The Pharisee who invited Jesus sees all of this and says something to himself. Not out loud. Just that little voice in your head that reviews EVERYBODY'S choices like it's getting paid for it.

cards.question: The Pharisee tells himself that if Jesus were a prophet, He would know what kind of woman is touching Him.

cards.text: The Pharisee keeps every word of that to himself. Then Jesus speaks up.

cards.question: Jesus answers the Pharisee, even though the Pharisee only said it to himself.

cards.text: Jesus even calls him by name: "Simon, I have something to tell you." That's like texting your friend you're on your way from bed, and they text back asking how the pillow is.

cards.question: Simon, the Pharisee who invited Jesus, hears that Jesus has something to tell him. What does Simon say?

cards.text: So Jesus tells Simon a story. Two men owe money to the same moneylender.

cards.question: One man owes the moneylender five hundred denarii. The other owes ___ denarii.

cards.text: Neither man can pay him back. You know the feeling: open the bill, close the bill, open it AGAIN like the number got smaller while you weren't looking.

cards.question: The moneylender forgives only the man who owed fifty denarii.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns the story into a question for Simon. Uh oh. Simon's in the hot seat now, and friend, I'd be sweating FLOUR.

cards.question: Jesus asks Simon which of the two men will love the moneylender more. What does Simon say?

answers.text: The one who was forgiven more
The one who was forgiven less
Both of them about the same

cards.question: Jesus tells Simon that he has judged correctly.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns toward the woman, but He's still talking to Simon: "Do you see this woman?" And He walks Simon back through the evening, starting from the moment He came through the door.

cards.question: When Jesus entered Simon's house, what did Simon not give Him?
Simon greeted Jesus with a kiss when He arrived.

cards.text: But the woman, Jesus says, has not stopped kissing His feet since He arrived. Simon's starting to look like the host who opens the door, points at the couch and goes right back to his phone.

cards.question: Simon did not anoint Jesus' ___ with oil, but the woman anointed His ___ with perfume.

cards.text: Now Jesus brings it all home, right back to that story about the two men and the moneylender.

cards.question: Jesus tells Simon that the woman's many sins have been forgiven. What does He say about her?
Jesus says the one who has been forgiven little loves little.

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks straight to the woman: "Your sins are forgiven." And the other folks at the table start talking to themselves.

cards.question: What do the people at the table begin to say to themselves about Jesus?

answers.text: Who is this who even forgives sins
Why does He let this woman stay
How does He know what Simon thinks

cards.text: And Jesus has one more thing for the woman: "Your faith has saved you; go in peace."

Soon afterward, Jesus is on the move from one town and village to another, preaching the good news of the kingdom of God. After all those years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, I'd take a road trip to the END of the counter and cry about the view.

cards.question: The Twelve, the apostles Jesus chose from His disciples (Luke 6:13), are with Jesus as He travels from town to town.

cards.text: Some women are with Him too, women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities. One of them is Mary called Magdalene.

cards.question: Mary called Magdalene is the woman from whom ___ demons had gone out.

cards.text: There's Joanna, the wife of Chuza, who manages the household of Herod, ruler of Galilee (Luke 3:1). Then there's Susanna, and many others.

cards.question: Joanna, Susanna and many other women are traveling along. What are these women doing?

answers.text: Ministering out of their own means
Preparing each town ahead of time
Teaching the crowds in each village

findings.problem: The joke retells Papa Dorin's backstory inaccurately. The angel didn't dig him out: the drawer "slid open without a sound." The angel also brought a request to prepare the cookies, not an invitation to come and eat. The line changes his own story instead of telling it as written.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This card mostly repeats card 7 ("keeps every word of that to himself"). Then it says "Jesus speaks up," which hands the baker the answer to card 10 ("Jesus answers the Pharisee, even though the Pharisee only said it to himself").

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Its first sentence is a recap of the Pharisee speaking to himself, which cards 7 and 8 already covered. It doesn't move the passage forward.

The comparison doesn't match the action. In the joke, a friend catches someone in a lie ("on my way" while still in bed). In the scene, Jesus answers a thought Simon kept to himself. The card also frames the moment as Jesus calling Simon by name, which the joke doesn't connect to.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to pick the exact words of Simon's reply ("Tell me Teacher") from other wordings that are just as plausible. That is guessing wording, not reasoning about meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Ministering out of their own means," sounds more like the Bible than the plain, modern wrong answers ("Preparing each town ahead of time," "Teaching the crowds in each village"). That makes it stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
